html:
SMTO-MEM-0041 — Knowledge vector service is unavailable

GUID: 98d4c65b-882d-58af-bb58-2aaab284a95b
Slug: knowledge-vector-database-unavailable
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • Knowledge keeps searchable copies of your documents and memories in a small database on the server. That database didn't answer, so searching and adding documents can't happen right now. This does not establish whether your files or other features are affected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Knowledge. If the status line says search is unavailable, select Check again next to it. This check can start the search database if it had stopped, so it may fix the problem on its own.
  2. Open System Health and select Check Knowledge. This tests whether the search database answers now, without changing anything.
  3. If either check keeps failing, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Ask them to repair the Knowledge installation on the server. A database that never answers usually needs a repair on the server computer.
  4. Once the checks pass, repeat your search. In Knowledge, select Retry failed jobs if any documents show Indexing failed. Documents that couldn't be processed while the database was down are tried again.

What success looks like

  • Check Knowledge passes and the Knowledge page shows Ready.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or re-upload your documents; that won't fix the search database.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Knowledge search database (the bundled local Qdrant service) did not become healthy after it was started, or a request to it failed or returned an error.

What this means

  • The local search database did not answer successfully. This does not establish whether source files or other features are available. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported vector_database_unavailable. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The vector service answers its authenticated status check.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • On the Knowledge page, Check again (GET /api/agent/rag/health) calls ensure_running and can start Qdrant; System Health's Check Knowledge only probes it and never starts it. On the server, check the Knowledge installation directory's runtime.json (loopback URL and api_key), that bin/qdrant can start with qdrant.yaml, and that the configured port is not used by another program. If the installation is damaged, stop the server, run python -m agent_runtime.rag.install in the application's Python environment with the same state configuration, start the server and check again.
  • Open System Health and run the Knowledge check. Ask the administrator to repair the Knowledge installation if the vector service remains unreachable.

Retry and execution caution

  • The vector service answers its authenticated status check.

How to verify the fix

  • The vector service answers its authenticated status check.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
